newsitem.title: INDIA: Templeton to launch Indian fixed-income fund.
newsitem.headline: Templeton to launch Indian fixed-income fund.

text.p: Templeton Asset Management (India) Pvt Ltd on Monday launched a mutual fund which will invest primarily in the country's debt market, senior officials said.

"We have growing confidence in the structure of the bond market," Douglas Lempereur, director for corporate development at Templeton Investment Counsel, Inc, told a news conference to announce the launch of the fund.
"Today we see the elements of a more mature bond market," Lempereur said, listing recent moves to boost the country's debt market including allowing foreigners to invest in government securities.

"India Income Fund" -- which opens on Monday through March 1 -- is the U.S. investment company's second domestic fund. Templeton launched "India Growth Fund" in August last year to invest in equities. The current net asset value of the equities fund is 10.33 rupees.
Templeton officials said they were not targeting any specific corpus for the new fund.
"There is no target. It's an open-ended fund and we plan to build on our assets over time," said Vijay Advani, president and CEO of Templeton in India.
Advani said Templeton was also registering several of its global bond funds in India to take advantage of new rules which ease investment in the debt market. He did not give any details.
The Franklin Templeton Group is one of the world's largest investment management companies with assets under management totalling $179 billion at the end of last year.
